clue.text: Posh man finally beginning to be indecent

parts.note: U is the old shorthand for upper-class speech and manners, hence posh

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word man

parts.note: to become something is to begin to be it, so beginning to be is becoming

explanation.surface: An upper-class gentleman is at last starting to behave improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' looks like a first-letter signal, but 'beginning to be' is one phrase meaning BECOMING; 'finally' takes the N from man.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both words describe behaviour that is improper or unseemly.

clue.text: Girl left holding old musical instrument

indicators.note: holding says the girl and left together wrap around the letter for old

parts.note: Vi, short for Violet, is a girl's name
O is the abbreviation for old, as in OE for Old English

explanation.surface: A girl ends up clutching an antique instrument after everyone else has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old musical instrument' wants to be the definition, but 'old' is needed for the O, which 'holding' puts inside VI and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bowed string instrument of the Renaissance, held upright, a forerunner of the violin family.

clue.text: A railway worker consuming fruit first, providing sustenance

indicators.note: first says the worker-and-fruit piece goes at the front, though the clue names the A and the railway before it
consuming says the worker swallows the fruit, taking it inside

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's standard worker, from the worker caste of the colony
a lime is a green citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A rail employee eats some fruit before handing out the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is about position, not a first letter: the worker-and-fruit piece leads, though the clue names the A and the railway before it; 'consuming' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the adjective means relating to nourishment, as in the canal that food travels down.

clue.text: Record points? A fencer may score them using this

definitions.text: A fencer may score them using this

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
compass points, here E for east twice over

explanation.surface: Someone logs the scores that a swordsman could notch up in a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' reads as a verb but is the noun EP, and each of the two 'points' is a compass point, E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the fencing sword whose hits win a bout, the word 'them' looking back to the points in the wordplay.

clue.text: Future monarch's charge concerning chap touring north

indicators.note: touring says the three pieces together travel round the letter for north

parts.note: a price is what is charged for something
N is the compass abbreviation for north
re means about or concerning, as in a memo heading
a gent is a chap, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: An heir to the throne's responsibility relates to a fellow travelling around the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' is the container, sending north inside the three-piece run; 'charge' reads as a duty or a ward, but means a cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an heir ruling for an incapacitated sovereign, as the later George IV did from 1811 before he was crowned.

clue.text: Pay back hanger-on in French city quarter

indicators.note: in says the hanger-on sits inside the name of the French city

parts.note: Reims is a cathedral city in the Champagne region of France
a bur is a prickly seed case that clings to clothes and fur, a literal hanger-on
a quarter is a compass point, here E for east

explanation.surface: Settle up with a sponger found in a district of a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city quarter' reads as one district, but splits: 'in' places the hanger-on inside the city alone, and the quarter is a separate compass point at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to repay someone money they have spent or lost.

clue.text: Way to introduce a fashionable spot

indicators.note: to introduce says the way comes in front of the two pieces that follow it

parts.note: St, short for street, is a way
in means in fashion, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: A method of launching a trendy venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mark or blemish left on a surface.

clue.text: Part of rehearsal — Salieri's dance music

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of the run-through is given over to the composer Salieri's dance number.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lively Latin American style with Cuban roots, played for dancing.

clue.text: Good Aussie sheep farm incorporating European development

indicators.note: incorporating says the pieces before it take the European letter inside them

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good, as on a grading scale
a station is the Australian term for a large sheep or cattle farm
E is the abbreviation for European, as in EU

explanation.surface: A fine Australian sheep ranch takes on a continental-style building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporating' slips E between G and STATION; 'development' reads as a building scheme but means growth before birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the growth of young in the womb, or of an idea, before it emerges.

clue.text: Fully earned diet regularly distributed at end of spring

indicators.note: at end of says the pieces named before it are attached after the word for spring

parts.note: a well is a spring, a natural source of water

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of diet, the first and third

parts.note: food that is distributed to diners is served

explanation.surface: A hard-won eating plan is handed out routinely as the season closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of spring' looks like a last-letter signal for G, but 'at end of' only places the other pieces after a spring of water; 'regularly' picks from diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: merited in full by effort or conduct.

clue.text: A wee bit backward providing info

indicators.note: backward says the A and the wee bit together are read from right to left

parts.note: a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: Someone a little slow is nonetheless supplying information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns A TAD around as one run, and 'A wee bit backward' reads as slightly slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: facts and figures; the definition is an informal shortening of information.

clue.text: Creative person possibly working on shift?

definitions.text: Creative person possibly working on shift?

parts.words: Creative person possibly working on shift?
parts.note: a shift is a loose straight frock as well as a spell of work, so this creator could be sewing one

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: someone who sews garments creates things, and a shift is a simple frock as well as a work period.

clue.text: Jarrow, where some would ultimately dock, perhaps

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: In the Tyneside shipbuilding town of Jarrow, some vessels would eventually tie up.
explanation.walkthrough: Jarrow is a shipbuilding town on the River Tyne in north-east England, so 'dock' reads as a berth for ships; it is the plant. 'ultimately' takes four last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: dock is a broad-leaved wild plant that gardeners root out, one unwanted kind among many.

clue.text: Current grudge against duke cutting income

indicators.note: cutting says the grudge and duke pieces slice into the word for income

parts.note: pay is the money earned from work, an income

indicators.note: against puts the grudge piece right up beside the duke's letter

parts.note: to grudge someone something is to resent it

explanation.surface: An ongoing resentment towards a nobleman is reducing someone's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting income' reads as a wage cut, but 'cutting' is the container and 'against' simply joins grudge and duke inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belonging to the time now, contemporary.

clue.text: Eg Derby University's elevated state

indicators.note: elevated, in a down clue, says the two pieces together are read upwards from the bottom

parts.note: a derby is the American name for a bowler, one example of a hat
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: The University of Derby, for one, enjoys a raised standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English city with a university, so 'Derby University' reads as one institution; it splits into HAT and U, which 'elevated' turns to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the fifty United States, in the Mountain West, with Salt Lake City as its capital.

clue.text: Pommy batsman's first run, leading to appeal?

indicators.note: leading to says the earlier pieces come ahead of the word for appeal
first takes the opening letter of the word batsman's

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run
it is an old word for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: An English cricketer scores his opening run, prompting a shout to the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an appeal is the fielders asking the umpire for a dismissal, which the surface plays on; here it is IT, sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are informal names, the definition an Australian one, for a person from the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Weep about woman's class with yen for liqueur

indicators.note: about says the word for weep goes round the woman's word

parts.note: to weep is to cry
her is the possessive for something that is a woman's
a brand is a particular kind or class of something
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Sob over a lady's lesson while craving a sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container; 'yen' reads as a craving but is the Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sweet fruit-flavoured spirit made with the red stone fruit.

clue.text: Like a service a graduate can provide

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
a tin is a can, the metal container

explanation.surface: Something resembling the help a degree-holder is able to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb 'is able to' but is the metal container, a TIN; the service is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival sense: relating to the morning office of the church, so resembling that act of worship.

clue.text: Supremely confident? Never thrown? Not so

indicators.note: thrown says the letters of the word before it are tossed into a new order

parts.note: not so, as in not so good, means less

explanation.surface: Someone utterly sure of themselves, never rattled? That's wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges NEVER into NERVE; the surface uses it to mean rattled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: calm and cool under pressure, showing no fear.

clue.text: Endlessly wow a city entertainments manager

indicators.note: Endlessly says the word for wow loses its last letter

parts.note: to wow an audience is to impress it
the final letter dropped from the word for wow
Rio de Janeiro, known as Rio, is a Brazilian city

explanation.surface: Keep on dazzling the person who runs a town's shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims the final S from IMPRESS; the surface uses it to mean without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who organises and promotes shows, concerts or operas.

clue.text: Officer's late unit broadcast about in French

indicators.note: about says the scattered letters go round the French word
broadcast means scattered, as seed is, so the letters of the two words before it are scattered

parts.note: en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: News of a commander's former squad was announced on air in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges LATE UNIT into LIEUTANT and 'about' wraps that round EN; the surface reads as a dead officer's unit reported on French radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a junior commissioned rank in the army or navy.

clue.text: Possibly the Sun King's disseminator of information?

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid, one example of a daily paper
a king is a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: Louis XIV, the Sun King, may have had his own spreader of news.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun King was Louis XIV of France, but the phrase splits: The Sun is a British tabloid, and a king is a chess piece, a MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a journalist, someone whose job is to spread the day's events in print.

clue.text: Informer with papers that hurt a deserted woman

parts.note: a grass is British slang for someone who informs to the police
identity papers are ID
ow is what someone cries to say that hurt

explanation.surface: A stool pigeon carries documents that injured an abandoned lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link here: it gives the W; 'that hurt' is the cry OW.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a wife whose husband is away for a long spell or has left her.

clue.text: Small amount of liquid female nurses landed on river

indicators.note: nurses says the female's name cradles the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Millie is a woman's name

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the landed word directly above the river's letter

parts.note: a bird that landed on a branch lit on it, the past tense of light
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A woman tends a tiny pool of fluid that came down by the stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' is the container, not a job; 'landed' is the past tense of light, as a bird alights on a branch, and 'on' stacks it over the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thousandth of a litre, a tiny metric measure of volume.

clue.text: Hospital doctor's back with substance right for injection

indicators.note: for injection says the substance and right pieces are pushed inside the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back of something
the gist of an argument is its substance

explanation.surface: A medic has returned with exactly the stuff needed for a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads as returned but is a noun, the hind part; 'for injection' is the container, putting two pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in British hospitals, a middle-ranking medic training as a specialist, below a consultant.

clue.text: Revolted by son's bloomers?

indicators.note: by puts the first piece right next to the son's letter

parts.note: to revolt is to rise up in rebellion, so revolted is rose
S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone is disgusted by their boy's baggy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' reads as old-fashioned underwear, or blunders; here it is whimsical for things that bloom. 'Revolted' is rebelled, not disgusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: plants that bloom, of which these thorny garden flowers are an example.

clue.text: Small child's slide

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A little one's playground chute.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to slip sideways out of control, as a car does on ice.

clue.text: A host that's always jolly involved

indicators.note: involved says the jolly's letters are wrapped up inside the word for always

parts.note: ay is an old or poetic word for always
jolly is British naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A party-giver who is invariably cheerful and gets stuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: A jolly is British naval slang for a Royal Marine; 'involved' is the container, wrapping an old poetic word for always round the marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a great multitude, as in a host of angels; originally a body of soldiers.
